title: WPSB/356/2014 of Praveen Chandra Goswami Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 356 of 2014
Praveen Chandra Goswami ......... Petitioner

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ......... Respondents
Present: Mr. Manoj Tiwari, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Sandeep
 Adhikari, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing Counsel for the State of
 Uttarakhand/respondent Nos. 1, 2 & 4.
 Mr. Vinay Kumar and Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocates for
 respondent No.3.

Coram : Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
JUDGMENT
Date: 3rd July, 2015
K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)

The writ petition has been filed seeking following
prayers :-
"i. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
 certiorari for quashing the impugned cancellation order
 dated 26.09.2014, passed by respondent No.1 and
 consequential orders dated 27.09.2014, passed by
 respondent No. 2 to 4 (Annexure No.9, 10 & 11 to the
 writ petition).
ii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
 mandamus restraining respondent Nos. 1, 2 & 4 from
 interfering with the functioning of the petitioner as
 District Employment Officer, Haridwar before
 completion of normal duration of posting i.e. 03
 years."
2. Petitioner and respondent No. 3 were appointed to the
posts of District Employment Officer in the year 2005. Petitioner
was posted in District Champawat, where he served upto
02.11.2007. Thereafter, he was transferred to Chamoli, where he
joined duties on 05.11.2007 and served till 16.08.2014. Therefore,
according to the petitioner, he has served in the hills throughout his

2
service career, whereas respondent No.3 was given first posting as
Special Employment Officer (Tribes) at Kalsi, District Dehradun.
He was transferred in 2007 to Champawat, but he did not join and,
according to the petitioner, by using his influence, he managed to
get himself transferred to Haridwar. According to the petitioner, he
has secured a right to be posted in Sugam area by serving at
Chamoli continuously for 6 years and 9 months. On 14.08.2014,
petitioner was transferred to Haridwar and respondent was
transferred in his place.
3. In short, the case of the petitioner that the respondent
did not join at Chamoli despite his transfer from Haridwar to
Chamoli by order dated 14.08.2014 and that is why the impugned
order was passed on 26.09.2014 by the 1st respondent and
consequential orders were also passed by respondent Nos. 2 and 4,
which are also impugned. By the same, there is a cancellation
affecting the transfer of petitioner to Haridwar and respondent No.3
to Chamoli; a curious thing about the cancellation is that it is
limited in point of time to one year.
4. Counter affidavit is filed by respondent No.3.
5. We heard learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner
Shri Manoj Tiwari,Shri Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for
respondent No.3 and also Mr. Pradeep Joshi, learned Government
Advocate for the State.
6. Petitioner has a case that in each time the 3rd
respondent is sought to be transferred. He has successfully evaded
his transfer. Petitioner has been working in the hilly areas for
almost entire period before his transfer to Haridwar and yet he is
visited by the order of temporary cancellation. The learned
Government Pleader is unable to justify the order of cancellation
and, that too, for a temporary period.

3
7. In the absence of reasons in conspectus of the facts,
which we have narrated for resorting to the cancellation of the
order, we would think that the cancellation is unjustified. In such
circumstances, the impugned orders will stand quashed. The writ
petition is allowed.
 (V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 03.07.2015 03.07.2015
P. Singh
